node_definition.done_when: A test in tests/test_a_read_can_ask_what_changed.py uses a fixture repository: a read with the observed_at of a previous read returns the one section whose declaration moved in a commit between the two, each section waiting on it whose readiness moved because of it, and exactly the one run whose classification changed in the fixture's transition stream. An unchanged project returns an empty change set with a new observed_at, and a since older than the stream's oldest row returns the full answer with full: true. The change set reads the plan files' git history through _plan_history in reckon/velocity.py and the producer's transition stream; no store, cursor or refusal is added, and the composition lives in a new module, reckon/change_set.py. On the base commit the three reads refuse or ignore since and the test fails there. The negative control is executed and logged. Gate: tests/test_a_read_can_ask_what_changed.py tests/test_mcp_tools.py. baseline_suite and after_suite are run with the project's armed suite command, PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_a_read_can_ask_what_changed.py, at the base and at the head, each log naming its revision, tree and literal command and ending EXIT=. Every test file that imports a production module the node changed adds no failure against a base arm: run both arms from git archive extractions on node-local disk with the main checkout's .env linked, record both logs, and re-run any id that differs between arms serially three times on each revision. ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the staged paths. Run the gate in the foreground on the fleet allocation.
